runtime.execution: Async Rust shell core (Tokio in examples), OS process groups/jobs and mutable shell state.
runtime.service_boundary: An application embeds a shell or invokes its executable; no provider or agent governor.

summary: Native shell composition, custom builtins and named jobs offer a strong OS integration reference, with explicit job-lifetime and timing limits.

inspection.scope: Read embedding examples, job states/wait/signal/foreground paths, history representation, timing and background compatibility cases.
inspection.limits: No full parser/Bash conformance audit; reference programs and test harness were not executed.

actions.name: Shell::run_string / invoke_function
actions.input: Shell source or named function, argv and FD execution parameters
actions.output: ExecutionResult/exit code, shell state and output streams

actions.name: Shell::builder().builtin
actions.output: Registered executable builtin with context/IO access
actions.lifecycle: Host construction; runtime uses registered implementation.
actions.authority: Embedding program; native change requires compilation

actions.name: Job::poll_done / wait / kill / move_to_foreground
actions.input: Job identity, signal or scheduling request
actions.output: Completion/stopped result, process group effects or error
actions.lifecycle: Ongoing job lifecycle; no native rebuild continuity.

evaluation.detail: Background cases use side effects after explicit wait; whole suite uses compatibility comparisons, but skipped exit-wait cases cannot prove lifecycle.

time_order.detail: Wall timing uses SystemTime and returns an error if clock goes backward; CPU accounting separate, no restart/paused-time semantics.

evidence.claim: A persistent shell defines/invokes a function and redirects file descriptors across calls.
Builtins execute against shell/context streams; builder registers native command implementation.
Jobs group tasks, process-group ID, command line, local ID and running/stopped/done state.
Poll/wait drain job tasks; background/foreground resume and kill act through process groups; background on nonstopped state is unimplemented.
History stores mutable command entries with IDs/timestamps and imports line-oriented command text; malformed UTF-8 may be skipped.
Timing uses SystemTime for wall delta and self/child CPU time; backward wall-clock subtraction can error.
Implicit-exit-wait cases are skipped; explicit wait cases observe filesystem side effects.

tests.focus: Background side-effect visibility after wait and shell exit.
tests.oracle: Explicit wait runs test -f then echo exists, compared by compatibility runner; implicit exit waits are skipped issue #1079.

strengths: Native embedding exposes ordinary shell state, function calls and descriptor-level IO.
Explicit job IDs/process groups make ongoing operations inspectable.
limits: Shell command history is not original audit.
Some background transition and implicit exit lifetime paths need targeted validation; wall timing is not monotonic.
arconaut_questions: Can a model receive durable operation handles while using ordinary shell composition?
How is job identity transferred or deliberately released when the consuming harness refits?
